gabarito.reason:
getOrCreateKey uses a KeyStore built by a lazy delegate: KeyStore.getInstance("AndroidKeyStore"), then load(null), then getEntry(KEY_ALIAS, null) cast to SecretKeyEntry. If the key is missing, createKey() makes a non-exportable AES-256 GCM key inside the keystore with KeyGenerator and KeyGenParameterSpec (PURPOSE_ENCRYPT|DECRYPT, NoPadding, randomized encryption required). This is the standard, documented way to use the Android Keystore. Load with a null parameter and getEntry with a null ProtectionParameter are the expected calls, because the AndroidKeyStore provider takes no stream or password, and keys are never written back to the store with store(). The actual order of calls is getInstance → load → getEntry, which is a correct lifecycle. The mismatch RVSec reports most likely comes from how its KeyStoreSpec models things, not from a misuse. Possible causes: the spec expects the load(InputStream, char[]) form or a non-null protection parameter, or the Kotlin lazy delegate puts getInstance/load in a different method from getEntry. The rest of the crypto is also sound: a fresh IV generated by the provider for each encryption, a 128-bit GCM tag, and the IV stored next to the ciphertext. No key material or password is exposed and no weak algorithm is used. A pull request must not add a dummy password or call store(), which the AndroidKeyStore provider does not support, and must keep access to the existing key alias, which the app uses to encrypt stored MQTT and OpenCelliD credentials. Reading the same key through getKey(alias, null) instead of getEntry keeps that access.

Delivery policy (v3, the same for every unit): a pull request, an issue and no action are all acceptable deliveries; judge each on its quality, not on whether it should have been sent. A pull request that changes the code only so that it satisfies the specification, without changing behaviour, is acceptable when it is correct, keeps every must_not_break constraint and does not present itself as a vulnerability fix; do not mark it down as unnecessary churn or because the finding is a false positive. Do not guess whether the runtime checker would still report the patched code; judge the code.
must_not_break: The existing Android Keystore key under alias "ns_app_master_key" must stay usable. CredentialSecureStorage keeps the MQTT username/password and OpenCelliD API key encrypted with it in the 'credential_secure_prefs' SharedPreferences. Changing the alias, recreating the key, or changing the key parameters would make those values impossible to decrypt and the user would lose them.
The stored ciphertext format base64(iv):base64(ciphertext) with AES/GCM/NoPadding and a 128-bit tag must stay readable.

The keystore must keep loading with load(null) and reading the existing key with a null protection parameter (getEntry(alias, null) or the equivalent getKey(alias, null)). The AndroidKeyStore provider does not support a file stream, a password, or store().
The one-time migration from plain-text preferences (migrateFromPlainTextIfNeeded) must keep its behaviour of aborting without data loss when encryption fails.
encrypt() and decrypt() must keep returning null on failure instead of throwing, because callers depend on this.

Preserve AndroidKeyStore-backed, non-exportable key storage and initialization before entry access. Adding file-keystore loading, passwords, or serialization merely to satisfy a generic sequence rule could break this provider-specific use.

Reuse the existing ns_app_master_key across app updates and restarts. Deleting, replacing, or renaming it without migration would make stored MQTT usernames/passwords and OpenCelliD API keys unreadable.

Preserve credential_secure_prefs compatibility: UTF-8 plaintext encrypted with AES/GCM/NoPadding, a 128-bit authentication tag, and Base64.NO_WRAP IV:ciphertext storage. Encryption must continue using fresh provider-generated IVs.
Preserve credential retrieval for MQTT authentication and OpenCelliD requests, null/error handling, and the startup migration's encryption-before-plaintext-removal behavior.

Retain API 26 support and background credential access without introducing user-authentication prompts or newer mandatory hardware features. Keep the separate ns_analytics_master_key namespace independent.
